subject: ophthalmology
title: Diseases of the sclera

steps.tx: **Episcleritis** is benign sectoral redness with mild irritation in young adults (simple diffuse blanching, or nodular with a tender movable nodule), settling with lubricants or short NSAIDs and never threatening vision. **Anterior scleritis** burns deeply with severe tenderness, sleep waking pain, violaceous non blanching vessels and photophobia, often in rheumatoid or granulomatosis vasculitis; diffuse, nodular and necrotising variants ascend in danger. Phenylephrine blanches episcleral but not deep scleral vessels, separating them at the slit lamp.
steps.say: Mild red patch that blanches is episcleritis; deep boring pain that never blanches is scleritis.

steps.tx: **Necrotising scleritis** thins sclera toward perforation (with inflammation, red and exquisitely painful, or scleromalacia perforans without inflammation in rheumatoid hands), risking staphyloma and needing systemic steroids with steroid sparing immunosuppression plus rheumatology. Scleritis workup hunts connective tissue disease, ANCA vasculitis, tuberculosis, syphilis and gout with bloods and chest imaging; infectious scleritis follows surgery or trauma with purulent nodules needing debridement and fortified therapy. Scleral patch grafting tectonically supports impending perforation.
steps.say: Melting white wall with deep pain needs systemic immunosuppression, not drops alone. Quiet melt in rheumatoid is scleromalacia.

steps.tx: **Posterior scleritis** hides behind a white eye with vision loss, pain on eye movement, choroidal folds, disc swelling and exudative detachment, mimicking tumours or Harada disease; B scan shows the **T sign** (fluid in sub Tenon space) clinching diagnosis. Treatment is systemic NSAIDs or steroids with immunosuppression for necrotising or recurrent disease. Anterior uveitis, cataract and raised pressure complicate prolonged inflammation. Children and young adults get idiopathic or infectious patterns more often than vasculitic ones.
steps.say: White eye losing vision with pain on moving: scan for posterior scleritis T sign.

steps.tx: **Staphyloma** bulges thinned sclera lined with uvea: anterior (corneal scar with iris incarceration), intercalary (limbal), ciliary (ciliary body), equatorial and posterior (pathological myopia with macular degeneration and retinal risk). High myopia with posterior staphyloma needs retinal surveillance. **Blue sclera** shows choroid through thin collagen in osteogenesis imperfecta (with fractures and deafness), Ehlers Danlos and Marfan patterns; acquired thinning blues in scleromalacia and high myopia. Scleral buckling supports retinal detachment repair externally.
steps.say: Uveal lined bulge is staphyloma; blue plus fractures is brittle bone disease.
